conservation.notes: Wikidata P141 gives least concern (Q211005). Wikipedia notes declines in parts of the southern range linked to winter ticks and parasites; the category is the Wikidata value, not a re-assessment.

human_tolerance.notes: Wikipedia reports collisions with vehicles as frequent in parts of North America and Scandinavia and describes 'urban moose' sightings in some areas. The Avoider rating and the absence of garden use are judgement, not a measured value.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Wikipedia: rutting and mating occurs in September and October; mature bulls stop feeding for about two weeks during the rut.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Wikipedia: cows usually bear one calf (twins if food is plentiful) in May or June after an eight-month gestation.

vocalizations.description: Heavy grunting from males during the rut, audible up to about 500 metres away (Wikipedia). Cooldown and loudness are judgement.
Wail-like calls from females during the rut, when both sexes call to each other (Wikipedia). Cooldown and loudness are judgement.

taxonomy.note: GBIF match Alces alces (Linnaeus, 1758), ACCEPTED, SPECIES, 2026-11-01; ITIS TSN 180703; Wikidata Q35517 carries the same GBIF, ITIS and NCBI (9852) identifiers. Genus Alces, family Cervidae, order Artiodactyla from GBIF. Odocoileus-style subspecies (A. a. gigas, A. a. americana) are not used: the record is the species.

common_names.note: Labels en moose, fr élan, de Elch, es Alces alces from Wikidata Q35517 (es is the scientific name, so it is dropped from common names in review if challenged).

range.note: Country list read from Wikipedia North America, Europe, and Asia sections: Canada and the US; Norway, Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Belarus, Ukraine, Czech Republic, Russia; Kazakhstan, Mongolia and northeastern China. Wikipedia names the Caucasus region without naming countries, so no Caucasus country is listed. Denmark (extinct, reintroduced 2016-17) and the New Zealand introduction are omitted; the introduced and invasive lists are left empty.

traits.limb_count.note: Four legs; the hooves and gait are standard for Cervidae.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk, trot, gallop and swim follow the Wikipedia description of moose as strong swimmers and their recorded running speed. The species-local program also represents shore wading with a walking gait; the schema has no dedicated wade gait.

traits.skin.note: Wikipedia: two-layer coat of hollow guard hairs and a woolly undercoat.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 356998.16 g (Alces alces, Ref_117), converted to kg (356.998, rounded to 357). It is a sex-pooled typical adult value.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia: males 380-700 kg and females 200-490 kg. The low end is the female minimum (200) and the high end is the male maximum (700).

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia: head-and-body length 2.4-3.1 m, tail 5-12 cm. Midpoints used: 2.75 m + 0.085 m = 2.835, rounded to 2.84 m. Nose-to-tail-tip is approximated by head-and-body plus tail.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Typical wild lifespan 8-15 years per the ADW Lifespan/Longevity section, 'Typical lifespan Status: wild 8 to 15 years'. Recorded as the midpoint of the stated range, 11.5 years. ADW separately reports that few moose live past 15 years in the wild and gives adult female survival as 95%; those statements describe survival, not typical lifespan. The 22-year range lifespan is a maximum and is not used. ADW text is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, accepted by project policy as a last resort; attribution is retained.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits gives Diet-PlantO 100 (plant, other) with no browse/graze split. Wikipedia: 'predominantly a browser', branches, twigs and dead wood form much of the winter diet, and 'as much as half' of the diet can be aquatic plants in other seasons. The 0.7 browse / 0.3 graze split is an authored allocation, not a measured one; aquatic plants are counted as graze because the schema has no aquatic category.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: solitary apart from cows with calves. group_size [1,2] (cow plus one calf) is a judgement from that statement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits: nocturnal 1 and crepuscular 1 (diurnal 0). Wikipedia (Newfoundland guidance): moose are most active at dusk and dawn. Crepuscular is the nearest enum value. Cathemeral is not used. Regional activity is in activity.regions.

traits.defense.note: Flee is the main response to threat. Wikipedia notes cows attack people near calves and bulls fight, so Mob is a secondary response that the record does not encode.

traits.wariness.note: judgement: 0.7. No source gives a flight distance for moose; a value near deer-like wariness was chosen and labelled as judgement.

habitat.use.note: Authored allocation: ground 0.9, aquatic 0.1. Wikipedia says moose wade or swim in lakes and ponds in hot weather and feed on aquatic plants, but gives no time share.

habitat.resources.note: browse (branches, twigs, deciduous browse), graze (aquatic and forb vegetation), shrub_thicket and shelter (forest cover, Wikipedia habitat section), water (lakes and ponds). Weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Avoider, road_mortality High from Wikipedia vehicle collision statements. uses_gardens false and the rating are judgement.

seasonal.phases.note: Rut September-October and calving May-June both come from Wikipedia's reproduction text. Phases are species-wide; no per-region phases are claimed.

behavior.note: Authored species-local fsm-moose-forager-v1: walk browse, gallop flee, drink and shelter rest; a walk-gait wade_feed state and a swim-gait swim_feed state are reachable in June-August (months [6, 7, 8]) when graze-tagged food and water are nearby. ADW says aquatic vegetation is consumed during summer; June-August is the authored northern-summer mapping for the US activity region. High sun (10-90 degrees) gates daytime rest, while feeding and movement can continue at dawn, dusk or night. The schema's food tags have generic graze but no aquatic-plant tag or water-bound food selector, so the swim state cannot guarantee the selected graze item is aquatic; see program description. Gait thresholds and distances are judgement.

look.note: judgement: proportions, palette and the palmate antler box are authored for the preview only. Antlers apply to bulls, and cows have none; the record shows the bull form.

vocalizations.bull_grunt.note: Wikipedia: males produce heavy grunting sounds that can be heard from up to 500 metres away, during the rut. cooldown_s and loudness are judgement.

vocalizations.cow_wail.note: Wikipedia: females produce wail-like sounds; both sexes call to each other during the rut. cooldown_s and loudness are judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: judgement: 'shelter' (forest cover where moose rest); Wikipedia describes moose using forest and cover but gives no resting-site tag.

seasonal.strategy.note: ActiveYearRound: Wikipedia describes year-round activity with seasonal movement between habitats and no hibernation or migration as a whole-population strategy.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Only the Adult stage is declared. Calves stay with the cow until the next calving (Wikipedia), but no per-stage durations are sourced.

traits.flight.note: None: a large non-flying cervid, by body plan. Wikipedia describes a terrestrial, wading and swimming animal, with no flight.

traits.nest_type.note: None: moose do not build nests, and no nest tag is used in the habitat block.

traits.senses.note: olfaction High from Wikipedia: the proboscis and olfactory column adapted for detection of moose urine and cows during the rut, and olfactory fine-tuning. Vision and hearing are not set; no openly licensed source gave a grade.

traits.size_class.note: Large: validator rule, mass_kg 357 is above 50 kg.
